To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
NHERF interacts with PMCA2 and is part of a complex that includes PMC2, HSP, and HER2 in lipid raft and actin-rich domains of the plasma membrane.
NHERF regulates the stability and signaling activity of the tyrsine kinase receptor HER2.
NHERF regulates the stability and localization of HER2 and PMCA2 in breast cancer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of PMCA2, NHERF1, and HER2 in breast cancer.
the role of the scaffolding protein NHE-RF1 in the control of HER2 stability and activity in breast cancer cells.
the molecular mechanisms that regulate the stability and function of the tyrosinkinase receptor HER2.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the scaffolding protein NHE1 regulates the stability of the tyrosin kinase receptor HER2 in mammary epithelial and breast cancer cells.
NHERF regulates the expression and signaling of the tyrosin-kinase HER2.
NHERF-1 acts with PMCa2 to regulate HER-2 signaling and membrane localization in breast cancers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the scaffolding protein Nherf1 regulates the expression and signaling of ErbB2 and the calcium pump PMca2 in breast cancer cells and that the expression of Nherf1 correlates with HER2 status and with increased mortality in breast cancer patients.
